stories.head: US and Iran trade strikes as tankers burn in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.say: The US and Iran have traded fresh strikes since Sunday, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards say six tankers have been set on fire. A third US aircraft carrier has reached the region.
stories.stand: Strikes widened on both sides as a third US aircraft carrier arrived and Iran ruled out nuclear inspections until the war ends.
body: The US and Iran have carried out widening strikes since Sunday 15 November. The US hit Iranian missile launchers in Bandar Lengeh and Sirik after Iranian forces attacked a US base in Bahrain, Euronews reported.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two more tankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, bringing the number set on fire since Sunday to six. The UK's maritime trade agency said one tanker was struck by an unknown projectile, causing an engine-room fire with no casualties.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt has joined two other US carrier strike groups, the first time since the Iraq war that three US carriers have been in the Middle East. Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said inspectors would not get access to nuclear sites until the war has permanently ended.

stories.head: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of 'attempted coup' over election-eve arrests
stories.say: Israel's opposition leaders say Benjamin Netanyahu attempted a coup, after reports his office prompted the arrest of three Arab party members before the October election. Likud denies it.
stories.stand: Reports say Netanyahu's chief of staff triggered police arrests of three Raam party members on the eve of the 27 October election.
body: Israel's Channel 12 reported that Benjamin Netanyahu's chief of staff, Ido Norden, filed a police complaint against members of the Arab party Raam on the eve of the 27 October election. Three Raam members were arrested and later released after police found the information unfounded.
Opposition leader Yair Lapid called it an attempted coup on Monday. Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main rival, said the caretaker prime minister cannot stay in office for another minute.

Netanyahu's Likud party denied the allegations and called Eisenkot's statement incitement. Neither bloc has the 61 seats needed to govern, and President Isaac Herzog has asked Eisenkot to try to form a government.

stories.head: Yemeni government forces pull back to defend Aden as Houthis advance
stories.say: Yemen's anti-Houthi forces have pulled back from near the Bab el-Mandeb strait to defend Aden, with Houthi fighters reported about sixty kilometres from the city.
stories.stand: The main anti-Houthi force withdrew from near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, saying securing Aden was its priority.
body: The Southern Armed Forces, the main anti-Houthi group, said on Sunday it was withdrawing from areas near the Bab el-Mandeb strait to secure Aden, the de facto seat of government.
Sources told AFP that Houthi fighters were holding positions about 60 kilometres west of Aden, ABC News reported. The Red Cross confirmed the Houthis had released 600 prisoners in Sanaa.
The withdrawal lets the Iran-backed Houthis consolidate control along the strait, CBS News reported. The World Food Programme says more than 18 million Yemenis face acute food insecurity.

stories.head: Widow of assassinated Haitian president Moise registers to run for president
stories.say: Martine Moise, widow of Haiti's assassinated president Jovenel Moise, has registered to run for president. She is one of thirty-three candidates for a vote set for July.
stories.stand: Martine Moise is one of 33 registered candidates for Haiti's first presidential election since 2016.
body: Martine Moise, widow of Haiti's slain president Jovenel Moise, has registered as a presidential candidate. Her name appeared on the electoral council's website on Sunday, Al Jazeera reported.
She is one of 33 registered candidates and one of three women. The first round is set for July next year. Haiti last held a presidential election in 2016.
Other candidates include former presidents Michel Martelly and Jocelerme Privert. Jovenel Moise was shot dead at his home in July 2021, and his wife was seriously wounded.

stories.head: Indonesia's president apologises to neighbours for wildfire haze
stories.say: Indonesia's president Prabowo Subianto has apologised to Singapore and Malaysia for haze from months of wildfires, the country's worst in eleven years.
stories.stand: Prabowo Subianto said seventeen company concessions have been revoked over the country's most intense fires in 11 years.
body: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto apologised to Singapore and Malaysia for haze from months-long wildfires, speaking at the ASEAN summit in Manila, his office said.
He said 17 company concessions had been revoked and 11 companies charged. Indonesia deployed 71,000 firefighters, and 16 people died fighting the blazes, he said.
The fires are Indonesia's most intense in 11 years, mainly in Sumatra, Borneo and Papua, Al Jazeera reported.

stories.head: ASEAN and China miss deal on South China Sea code of conduct
stories.say: Talks between Southeast Asian nations and China on a South China Sea code of conduct have ended without a deal, though the Philippines says about eighty per cent is agreed.
stories.stand: About 80% of the draft is tentatively agreed, but whether the code is legally binding remains open.
body: ASEAN and China failed to finish talks on a South China Sea code of conduct in Manila, Philippine Foreign Minister Theresa Lazaro said on Sunday.
She said about 80% of the draft was tentatively agreed, but key issues remain, including whether the code would be legally binding. The Philippines had pledged a deal by the end of 2026.
ASEAN also extended its ban on Myanmar's leader attending its summits, saying the country had not complied with a 2021 peace plan.

stories.head: Trump flies to Asia and says he could meet Kim Jong-un in China
stories.say: Donald Trump has left for Asia, starting in Manila before three-way talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen. He says he may also meet Kim Jong-un.
stories.stand: The president heads to Manila, then to Shenzhen for the first three-way talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
body: Donald Trump said on Monday he may meet North Korea's Kim Jong-un in China this week, speaking as he left the White House for Asia.

He arrives in the Philippines first, where the White House says he will sign a trade deal with Thailand. He then travels to Shenzhen for the APEC summit and three-way talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
US officials said the talks would focus on nuclear weapons. Trump said denuclearisation, the wars in Iran and Ukraine, and trade would come up.

stories.head: Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker
stories.say: Estonia will close its border crossings with Russia after an attempted arson attack on a drone maker, which it says was ordered by Russian military intelligence.
stories.stand: Eight people were detained over an attempted arson attack on Threod Systems that Tallinn blames on Moscow.
body: Estonia will close its border crossings with Russia, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna announced on Sunday. He did not say how long the closure would last.

It follows an attempted arson attack on defence company Threod Systems, a drone maker. Eight people were detained overnight, and Estonian authorities said the attack was ordered by Russia's GRU military intelligence.
Estonia has three open crossings with Russia: Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula. A Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman called the plan Russophobia, Al Jazeera reported.

stories.head: Pope Leo demands justice for murdered Amazon defenders in Peru
stories.say: Pope Leo has demanded justice for Indigenous leaders killed defending the Amazon, speaking to missionaries and Indigenous groups on the Ucayali River in Peru.
stories.stand: Speaking in Pucallpa, the Pope urged Catholics to oppose deforestation and pollution from gold and oil production.
body: Pope Leo XIV demanded justice for environmental defenders killed while protecting the Amazon, speaking on Sunday in Pucallpa, Peru, to Indigenous representatives and missionaries.
He said many Indigenous leaders had been murdered for defending their territories, and urged Catholics to oppose deforestation and pollution from gold and oil production.
Campaign groups estimate 57 environmental defenders were murdered in Peru between 2010 and 2024. The visit is part of a 12-day tour of South America.

stories.head: Guadalajara cartel founder Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies aged 80
stories.say: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, who co-founded Mexico's Guadalajara cartel and was jailed over the 1985 murder of a US drug agent, has died aged eighty.
stories.stand: He was convicted over the 1985 murder of US drug agent Enrique Camarena and died two days after leaving prison for hospital.
body: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, co-founder of Mexico's Guadalajara cartel, died on 15 November aged 80, the Jalisco state security ministry said. It said he suffered multiple organ failure, two days after being moved from prison.
He was convicted over the February 1985 murder of US Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique Camarena. He was arrested in April 1989 and was serving a 40-year sentence.
He co-founded the Guadalajara cartel with Rafael Caro Quintero. The Sinaloa cartel later emerged from it, CBS News reported.

stories.head: Record numbers of migrants reach Spain's Canary Islands
stories.say: Nearly two thousand two hundred migrants reached Spain's Canary Islands by boat over two days, most landing on the small island of El Hierro. Spain has declared a migration emergency there.
stories.stand: Spain declared a migration emergency on the islands as daily arrivals approached or passed the 2020 record.
body: Nearly 2,200 migrants reached the Canary Islands by boat over two days, Spain's maritime rescue service said on Sunday. Most landed on El Hierro, an island of about 12,000 people, ITV News reported.
Spain declared a migration emergency on the islands last week as arrivals rose, particularly from sub-Saharan Africa. Al Jazeera said more than 9,000 people have arrived since the start of November.
Most boats leave from Mauritania. The International Organization for Migration recorded at least 450 deaths on the Atlantic route in the first 10 months of 2026.

stories.head: Five EU countries agree deportation hubs in Rwanda
stories.say: Greece, Denmark, Germany, Austria and the Netherlands have agreed a deal with Rwanda to set up deportation hubs for migrants, with pilot centres expected by mid twenty twenty-seven.
stories.stand: The first pilot centres are expected by mid-2027, though France and Spain oppose the plan.
body: Greece, Denmark, Germany, Austria and the Netherlands announced a partnership with Rwanda to set up return hubs for irregular migrants, Euronews reported. The first pilot centres are expected to be running by mid-2027.
The first facility is expected to hold about 100 people, according to people familiar with the talks. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen called the deal a game changer.
Nineteen of the 27 EU governments back the approach, while France and Spain have voiced opposition. Rwanda's interior minister said the country would respect fundamental rights.

stories.head: Australian MP Helen Haines leaves hospital after losing both legs
stories.say: Australian independent MP Helen Haines has left hospital four weeks after being hit by a car in Wangaratta, an attack that cost her both legs. A man has been charged.
stories.stand: The independent MP was hit by a car in Wangaratta on 19 October; a 43-year-old man has been charged.
body: Independent MP Helen Haines, 65, left Melbourne's Alfred Hospital on Monday, four weeks after she was airlifted there, Euronews reported. Her injuries led to the amputation of both legs.

She was hit by a Toyota Land Cruiser on 19 October while standing near her car in Wangaratta. Police have charged Brendan Nugent, 43, with offences including dangerous driving and harming a public official. The charges have not been tested in court.
Haines said she had moved into the rehabilitation stage of her recovery. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he is in regular contact with her family.

stories.head: Peers warn UK is 'seriously underprepared' for emergencies
stories.say: A House of Lords committee says the UK is seriously underprepared for emergencies such as cyber attacks and extreme weather, and wants a cabinet minister for resilience within six months.
stories.stand: The Lords committee says small food and medicine stockpiles leave the country exposed to supply shocks.
body: The House of Lords National Resilience Committee says the UK is seriously underprepared for emergencies and threats including cyber attacks and extreme weather.

It says limited stockpiles of food and medicine leave the country exposed, and notes the UK has no domestic antibiotic makers. It wants a Cabinet minister solely responsible for resilience within six months.
It also recommends scrapping plans to switch off digital terrestrial television. The Cabinet Office said it would carefully review the report.

It followed a yellow ice warning on Monday morning across much of Scotland and parts of northern England. A Met Office meteorologist warned of potentially hazardous travelling conditions.
The UK Health Security Agency has issued a yellow cold-health alert for the North West, North East, and Yorkshire and the Humber until 9am on Thursday.

stories.head: Women convicted under old abortion law automatically pardoned
stories.say: Women convicted of ending their own pregnancies under an eighteen sixty-one law are being automatically pardoned, following last year's vote to decriminalise abortion.
stories.stand: The pardons follow last year's vote to repeal part of the 1861 Offences Against the Person Act.
body: Women convicted of illegally ending their pregnancies under a Victorian law were to be automatically pardoned on Monday, the government said. They do not need to apply.
Women given a police caution will also be pardoned, and those arrested or investigated will have the details removed from their records, Euronews reported.
It follows Parliament's vote last year to decriminalise abortion by repealing a section of the 1861 Offences Against the Person Act. The government did not say how many women are affected.

stories.head: Two die in Leeds after car chased by police hits another vehicle
stories.say: Two young people from York have died in Leeds after a car being chased by police crashed into theirs early on Sunday. Four people have been arrested.
stories.stand: A 39-year-old man and three teenagers were arrested; the police watchdog is investigating.
body: Two people died after a BMW being pursued by police hit a Volkswagen on Gelderd Road in Leeds early on Sunday, West Yorkshire Police said.
The Volkswagen's 22-year-old driver died at the scene and a 23-year-old passenger died in hospital. Both were from York.

A 39-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and drug-driving. Three teenage passengers were also arrested. The Independent Office for Police Conduct has begun an investigation.

stories.head: Reports of AI-made child abuse images up more than 8,400% in two years
stories.say: Reports of AI-generated child abuse material passed on by tech firms rose from about four thousand seven hundred in twenty twenty-three to over four hundred thousand last year.
stories.stand: Edinburgh-based Childlight says reports to a US clearing house rose from about 4,700 to more than 400,000.
body: Reports of AI-generated child sexual abuse material passed by tech companies to a US clearing house rose from around 4,700 in 2023 to more than 400,000 in 2025, research group Childlight said.
Childlight, hosted at the University of Edinburgh, said that was a rise of more than 8,400%. It estimates more than 300 million children a year face some form of technology-facilitated abuse.
The figures are in its 2026 Into the Light Index, presented to a global summit on ending violence against children, ITV News reported.

stories.head: Asking prices fall more than usual in November, Rightmove says
stories.say: Average asking prices for homes coming to market fell one point eight per cent this month, Rightmove says, a bigger drop than is usual for November.
stories.stand: New sellers' prices dropped 1.8% to £364,270, against a ten-year November average fall of 1.1%.
body: Average asking prices for newly listed homes fell 1.8% this month to £364,270, according to Rightmove. The ten-year average fall for November is 1.1%.
Prices were 0.2% lower than a year earlier, and every region saw a monthly fall. Scotland had the strongest annual growth, at 3.8%.
In London, average asking prices fell 1.8% to £662,118, reversing much of October's 2.5% rise, PrimeResi reported.

stories.say: King Charles has opened Ribble House, the new headquarters of the National Cyber Force, at Samlesbury in Lancashire.
stories.stand: The NCF, run by GCHQ and the Ministry of Defence, now has its home at Samlesbury.
body: King Charles III officially opened Ribble House, the National Cyber Force's new headquarters in Samlesbury, Lancashire, the government said.

The force is a partnership between GCHQ and the Ministry of Defence, also drawing on MI6 and the Defence Science and Technology Laboratory. Its work includes countering state threats and disrupting online criminals.
The King met GCHQ director Anne Keast-Butler during the visit.

body: An 11-metre object called 1998 KY26 is passing near Earth, and its path and speed cannot be fully explained by the gravity of the Sun or Earth, Euronews reported.

Astrophysicist Avi Loeb and colleagues propose it could be Phobos 1, a Soviet spacecraft launched in July 1988 that lost contact on its way to Mars. Other studies have suggested it is a dehydrated asteroid or a dark comet.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency is monitoring the object and it poses no known threat. Japan's Hayabusa2 is due to reach it in July 2031.

stories.stand: ESA's probe is studying the double asteroid four years after NASA's DART spacecraft struck its moonlet.
body: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has sent its first close-up image of the asteroid Didymos, showing boulders, craters and grooves, ScienceDaily reported.
Didymos is 780 metres across; its moonlet Dimorphos, 151 metres across, was struck by NASA's DART spacecraft in September 2022, shortening its orbit by about 33 minutes.
ESA says more detailed images of both asteroids are due on 25 November.

stories.head: Tiny animals found living inside deep-sea metal nodules
stories.say: Scientists in Bremen found more than four thousand tiny animals living inside metal-rich nodules on the Pacific seabed, with one nodule home to two hundred and forty-five.
stories.stand: Bremen researchers say deep-sea mining could wipe out habitats that take a million years to grow.
body: Researchers at the University of Bremen's MARUM centre examined 244 polymetallic nodules from the Pacific's Clarion-Clipperton Zone and found 4,139 animals living in their cracks, ScienceDaily reported.
Each nodule held an average of 17 animals, and one held 245. The communities differed from those in the surrounding mud.
The nodules grow only a few millimetres in a million years. The researchers say deep-sea mining could remove habitats that cannot recover within a human lifetime. The study is in Scientific Reports.

stories.head: Delft physicists control the nuclear spin of a single atom with radio waves
stories.say: Physicists at Delft have used radio waves to flip the magnetic spin of a single atom's nucleus, a result they say their previous understanding did not predict.
stories.stand: The team adapted double magnetic resonance to work on one atom using a scanning tunnelling microscope.
body: Physicists at Delft University of Technology used radio waves to directly control the magnetic spin of a single atom's nucleus, ScienceDaily reported.

The team, led by Sander Otte, applied two signals to one atom at once with a modified scanning tunnelling microscope. The nuclear spin flipped even when it was largely disentangled from the electron spin.
The researchers say the mechanism is not yet understood and the work is an early step rather than a usable quantum memory. It is published in Nature Communications.

body: Astronomers at the International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research found a white dwarf that rotates every eight minutes and emits radio pulses, ScienceDaily reported.

The system was found with the Murchison Widefield Array in Western Australia. The study is in Nature Astronomy.

stories.head: Ancient virus helped silence a brain gene in chimpanzees, study finds
stories.say: Researchers at Lund University say an ancient virus switched off a gene in chimpanzees that stays active in humans, which may help explain differences between our brains.
stories.stand: Lund University researchers say a viral insertion switches off LINC00662 in chimpanzees but not humans.
body: An ancient virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago left an insertion that switches off a gene called LINC00662, Lund University researchers found, ScienceDaily reported.
The gene stays active in humans. Removing the viral sequence from chimpanzee cells with CRISPR reactivated it.
Disabling the gene in human brain organoids reduced activity of genes linked to nerve cell development. The study is in Science Advances.

body: Researchers at the University of California, Berkeley have mapped how brain circuits in mice drive growth hormone release during sleep, Euronews reported. The study is published in Cell.
In non-REM sleep, cells that inhibit growth hormone become less active. In REM sleep, the cells involved act together to boost it further.
The rising hormone also stimulated a brainstem region involved in alertness. The mechanism has not been confirmed in humans.

stories.head: US loses measles-free status as cases pass 5,700
stories.say: The United States has lost its measles elimination status, held since two thousand, after more than five thousand seven hundred cases this year. Ten deaths have been linked to the disease.
stories.stand: A Pan American Health Organization panel found measles had become established in the US; 10 deaths have been reported this year.
body: The US has lost the measles elimination status it held since 2000, after a Pan American Health Organization expert group found the disease had established a foothold, Euronews reported.
There have been 5,739 cases so far in 2026, according to a Johns Hopkins University tracker, up from 2,286 last year. State health departments report 10 measles deaths this year.
Under PAHO's rules a country loses the status if measles spreads uninterrupted for at least a year. The outbreak began in West Texas in early 2025.

stories.say: A study of over thirteen hundred older adults followed for up to nineteen years found each extra hour of daytime sleep was linked to about a thirteen per cent higher risk of death.
stories.stand: The 19-year study found an association, not proof that napping causes harm.
body: A study of 1,338 older adults followed for up to 19 years found each extra hour of daytime sleep a day was linked to about a 13% higher risk of death, ScienceDaily reported.

The research, led by Brigham and Women's Hospital and published in JAMA Network Open, shows correlation, not causation, the lead author said.

stories.say: MIT researchers found that short bursts of quiet pink noise during deep sleep strengthened the fluid waves that flush the brain, in a study of fourteen volunteers.

The study, in Science Translational Medicine, did not directly show more waste was removed or that sleep quality improved.

stories.stand: HHS recently changed its recommendation to allow far more of the compound 7-OH in products.
body: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention detected kratom in more than 5,000 overdose deaths between 2020 and 2024, CBS News's 60 Minutes reported.

In July the federal government said it would restrict 7-OH and three related substances found in kratom products. Last month the Department of Health and Human Services changed course, including a 20-fold increase in the amount of 7-OH allowed.
HHS said neither political contributions nor outside pressure influenced the decision. The FDA warns against using kratom, citing risks including liver toxicity and seizures.

stories.head: Burnham backs Saturday 3pm TV blackout
stories.say: Andy Burnham has backed keeping football's Saturday three p.m. TV blackout, saying it protects lower-league clubs, and criticised Premier League kick-off times.
stories.stand: The prime minister urged caution before changing a rule in place since the 1960s.
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham backed the 3pm Saturday blackout on live TV football and urged caution before changing it, saying it protects the income of lower-league clubs, ITV News reported.
He also criticised Premier League kick-off times for not taking travelling supporters into account.
Of the 380 Premier League fixtures, 270 are shown live by TNT Sports or Sky Sports.

stories.head: Popovic's Socceroos future uncertain after Asian Cup postponement
stories.say: Socceroos coach Tony Popovic admits his future is uncertain after the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia was postponed because of conflict there.
stories.stand: His contract runs only to Wednesday's friendly with Jordan, moved to Doha over security concerns.
body: Socceroos coach Tony Popovic admits his future is uncertain after the Asian Cup, due in January in Saudi Arabia, was postponed because of conflict in the host nation, ABC News reported.
Popovic has no contract beyond Wednesday's friendly against Jordan, which was moved to Doha after players raised security concerns.
He said he would hold talks with Football Australia in the next couple of months.
